title: Alternate Day Work Schedules
tagline: Year 3 — Workers taking turns by day, cycle work and the last partial cycle

introduction.overview: In an alternate-day schedule the workers do not work together; they take turns, one on each day, in a fixed order. The work done in one complete cycle is the sum of their daily outputs. The job is finished after some whole number of cycles plus a partial last cycle. The method is to find the work per cycle, count the full cycles that fit before the job is completed, and then see who finishes the remainder.
introduction.placementRelevance: Alternate-day work questions are commonly asked in company aptitude rounds as a harder variant of time and work, usually with two or three workers.
introduction.realWorldContext: Shift rosters, rotating machine operators and duty rotations between teams are alternate-day schedules.

learningObjectives: Compute the work done in one cycle of the rotation
Find the number of full cycles before the job ends
Identify who completes the last part
Handle three or more workers in rotation
Handle changes of order or different starting workers

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Use LCM units so each worker's daily output is a whole number. Total units = LCM of the times.

coreDefinitions: Cycle: one complete round of the rotation (each worker works one day).
Cycle output: the sum of the daily outputs of all workers in the cycle.
Full cycles: the number of complete rounds before the remaining work is less than one cycle output.
Last partial cycle: the final days in which the remaining work is finished.
Alternate with a start: the order matters when the job ends part-way through a cycle.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: A rotation turns many days into repeated blocks. After you account for as many complete blocks as possible, only a short tail remains, and the tail is solved by looking at one worker at a time.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Convert to units, add the daily outputs for the cycle output, divide the total by it to find full cycles (keeping the remainder), then run the tail day by day.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Cycle output
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Σ daily outputs of the workers in the rotation
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: A 3 + B 2 = 5 units per two days

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Full cycles
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: Leave room for the finishing day.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Tail
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: 5 units left: A does 3, B does 2

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Total days
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: (cycles × workers in a cycle) + days in the tail

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Finishing before the cycle ends
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: If the remainder ≤ the first worker's output, the first worker finishes it

mainNarrative: Choose units. If A takes 20 days and B takes 30 days, take the job as 60 units: A does 3 units a day and B does 2. In a two-day cycle (A then B) they do 5 units.
Count full cycles. 60 ÷ 5 = 12 exactly, so after 12 cycles (24 days) the job is done, with B finishing on the last day. If A starts, A works first in every cycle.
Handle the tail carefully. For A = 12 days and B = 18 days with 36 units, A does 3 and B does 2. A cycle yields 5 units, 7 cycles (14 days) yield 35, and the remaining 1 unit is done by A on day 15.

The order of work can change the total time. If B starts in the same example, B does 2 then A does 3 in each cycle; after 7 cycles 35 units are done and B finishes the last unit on day 15 as well. When the remainder is small enough for the first worker, the starter finishes.
For three workers, the cycle has three days. A, B, C with outputs 4, 3, 2 do 9 units per cycle. A 40-unit job is done in 4 full cycles (36 units, 12 days) plus 4 more units: A does 4 on day 13.

deepDiveAspects.title: When the starter changes the answer
deepDiveAspects.content: If the job ends exactly after a complete cycle, the answer is the same whichever worker starts. If it ends part-way, the answer may differ by a day.

deepDiveAspects.title: Leave and join
deepDiveAspects.content: If one worker is absent in a cycle, drop his output for that cycle and continue with the others.

solvedExamples.title: Two workers in turn
solvedExamples.question: A can do a job in 12 days and B in 18 days. They work on alternate days, A first. In how many days is the job finished?

steps.title: Units
steps.explanation: Total = 36. A does 3 and B does 2 per day.

steps.title: Cycle
steps.explanation: 3 + 2 = 5 units per two days. After 7 cycles (14 days) 35 units are done.

steps.title: Tail
steps.explanation: 1 unit is left: A does it on day 15.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: A starts the next cycle and needs only 1 unit.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Dividing 36 by 5 and rounding up to 8 cycles (16 days).

solvedExamples.title: Exact cycles
solvedExamples.question: A takes 20 days and B takes 30 days. They work on alternate days, starting with A. When is the job finished?
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: Check whether the job ends on a cycle boundary.

steps.title: Cycle
steps.explanation: 5 units per two days, so 60/5 = 12 full cycles.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The job ends exactly after B's day.

solvedExamples.title: Three workers
solvedExamples.question: A, B and C can do 4, 3 and 2 units of a 40-unit job per day respectively and work in turn, A first. How many days does the job take?

steps.title: Tail
steps.explanation: 4 units left: A does 4 on day 13.

shortcutMethods.title: Cycles then tail

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Divide the total by the cycle output, keep the full cycles, and finish the remainder day by day.

rulesForApplication: Units per day for each worker.
Remainder ≤ first worker's output → he finishes.

commonMistakes.whyItHappens: Using the ceiling for the last cycle.
commonMistakes.howToAvoid: Run the tail day by day.

commonMistakes.whyItHappens: Assuming the starter does not matter.
Adding the days of A and B.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: The answer must be between half the shorter time and the longer time of the two.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Write the cycle output and the tail on two lines.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: A day-by-day check of the tail removes most errors.
